chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd bin Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Bakr bin Salih al-Razi, from Abu al-Salt al-Khurasani, who said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about faith, so he said:
Faith is a contract in the heart, utterance by the tongue, and action by the limbs; faith is not except like this.
ai.seo_question: What are the three components of faith according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) defines faith (iman) as a tripartite concept comprising internal conviction (heart), verbal declaration (tongue), and physical practice (limbs), establishing that all three components are necessary for faith to be complete. This hadith from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* underscores the Shia emphasis on the integration of belief and action, distinguishing it from views that prioritize mere verbal confession or internal assent alone. The inclusion of 'work of the limbs' highlights the practical manifestation of faith, a key theme in Shia jurisprudence and theology.

en.basel-kadem: 2.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammed, from Bikr bin Saleh al-Razi, from Abu’s-Silt al-Khurasani, that he said: I asked al-Rida, peace be upon him, about faith, so he said:
Faith is a contract in the heart, uttering by the tongue and act with the limbs; faith is by nothing except like this.
